name: Train on SageMaker from S3 (data never enters the VM)
desc: UNLOAD a huge Athena result to S3, train sm_train straight off the S3 pointer, then load + score — for data too big to pull into the sandbox

## 📦 Train on SageMaker from S3 — the VM never touches the data

The *managed training* recipe still pulls your rows into a DataFrame first (`read_athena(...) → sm_train(df, ...)`), so it's bounded by the sandbox's memory. When the **training set itself is too big to live in the VM**, flip the data flow around:

1. **`unload_athena_to_s3(sql)`** — Athena runs the query on its OWN fleet and writes the result straight to S3. No rows come back to the VM; you get a lightweight **pointer** (an `UnloadResult`: `.s3_uri`, `.file_count`, `.total_bytes`).
2. **`sm_train(pointer, target, task=...)`** — the SageMaker instance reads the training set **directly from S3**. The VM only samples ONE file to infer the feature split; the full dataset never materializes in the sandbox.

```mermaid
graph LR
  Q["Athena SELECT / JOIN"] -->|unload_athena_to_s3| S3["Parquet in S3 (VM-free)"]
  S3 -->|pointer| T["sm_train(pointer, task=…)"]
  T -. managed compute reads S3 directly .-> J["SageMaker Training Job"]
  J -->|sm_load_model| M["model in VM"]
  M -->|predict_batch| P["scored rows"]
```

**When to reach for this:** `read_athena(...)` into a DataFrame would blow the VM's memory, or you're prepping millions of rows / a big JOIN. For data that comfortably fits the VM, the plain *managed training* recipe (DataFrame → `sm_train`) is simpler.

**Two things to remember for the pointer path:**
- It **requires `task=`** (`"classification"` or `"regression"`) — the VM can't infer it without reading the data.
- It's **scikit-learn only** today (every estimator — random_forest/xgboost/lightgbm/… — works, same script-mode path). `data_format=` is auto-detected (UNLOAD writes Parquet by default).

**Cost & timing:** the UNLOAD is an Athena query (scanned-bytes billing, seconds–minutes); the training job takes minutes (instance spin-up ~3–4 min) and bills only while it runs. Nothing stands after it finishes — see the *Deploy a real-time endpoint* recipe to host the model.

# 1) UNLOAD a (potentially huge) Athena result straight to S3 — Athena transforms
#    and writes server-side, so NOT A SINGLE ROW enters the VM. Cross-database /
#    cross-catalog JOINs work exactly like read_athena (qualify as db.table).
#    Returns a POINTER (UnloadResult), not a DataFrame.
prep = unload_athena_to_s3('''
    SELECT o.order_id, o.total, o.quantity, o.shipping_country, o.payment_method,
           p.category, p.brand, p.price,
           CASE WHEN e.status = 'returned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS returned
    FROM microvm_demo_db.orders o
    JOIN microvm_demo_db.products p   ON o.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN microvm_demo_iceberg.order_events e ON o.order_id = e.order_id
''')
print(prep.s3_uri)
print(f"{prep.file_count} file(s), {prep.total_bytes/1e6:.1f} MB written by Athena")

### Alternative: UNLOAD from a SQL cell

The step above uses the Python helper because it hands back a `prep` pointer the next cell needs. You can also run an UNLOAD **directly in a SQL cell** — same engine, result is the file list:

```sql
UNLOAD (
  WITH labelled AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.total, o.quantity, o.shipping_country, o.payment_method,
           p.category, p.brand, p.price,
           CASE WHEN e.status = 'returned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS returned
    FROM microvm_demo_db.orders o
    JOIN microvm_demo_db.products p ON o.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN microvm_demo_iceberg.order_events e ON o.order_id = e.order_id
  )
  SELECT * FROM labelled
) TO 's3://<your-artifact-bucket>/unload/returnrisk/' WITH (format='PARQUET')
```

Omit the `TO '...'` and a fresh unique prefix is chosen for you. To then train from it, pass the S3 prefix string to `sm_train` (`sm_train('s3://.../unload/returnrisk/', target='returned', task='classification')`).

# 1b) (optional) PEEK at what landed — read just the part files back WITHOUT loading
#     the whole set. Athena UNLOAD writes EXTENSIONLESS parquet, so pass
#     format='parquet' (auto-detect skips files with no extension). Keep this to a
#     small sample; the point of the pointer path is to NOT pull the full data in.
# sample = read_s3_prefix(prep.s3_uri, format='parquet')
# print(sample.shape); sample.head()

# 2) SUBMIT training straight from the S3 pointer — NON-BLOCKING, returns a handle in
#    ~seconds. The SageMaker instance reads the data from S3; the VM only samples ONE
#    file to infer the feature split. The pointer path REQUIRES task=.
#    Optional: estimator= (random_forest default · gradient_boosting · xgboost ·
#    lightgbm · logistic · linear · ridge), instance= (e.g. 'ml.m5.2xlarge'),
#    features=/categorical=/numeric=, data_format= ('csv'|'parquet', auto by default).
job = sm_train(prep, target="returned", task="classification", estimator="xgboost")
print("submitted:", job)

# 3) POLL until it finishes — RE-RUN this cell every ~30s. Status walks
#    'InProgress (Nm elapsed)' → 'Completed (Nm)' (or 'Failed: <reason>').
#    Only move on once it reads Completed.
print(sm_training_job_status(job))

# 4) Load the finished model into the VM. sm_load_model WAITS for the job, then
#    returns a complete scikit-learn Pipeline that takes RAW rows (plain joblib.load —
#    no rewrap). xgboost/lightgbm libs are auto-installed in the VM on load.
model = sm_load_model(job)
model_info(model)

# 5) Score. predict / predict_batch accept EITHER the loaded model OR the job handle
#    (auto-resolved via sm_load_model) — same surface for local and SageMaker models.
#    Score a bounded hold set you CAN fit in the VM (don't pull the full S3 set back):
hold = read_athena("SELECT * FROM microvm_demo_db.orders LIMIT 5000")
scored = predict_batch(job, hold, output_col="prediction")
scored.head()
